answer: An identity must be at least 6 epochs old on the sable ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. Because the age is read from the walnut checkpoint rather than self-declared, the karst audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. Running a farm as a result means funding each extra identity through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent burns once and never again. That is 30 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
